differences.what: the round tower: the photograph's stands on the 18th Street flank about 8 m back from the front, where the 1911 sheet draws a bump in the north wall, its eaves about 12.9 m and its cone to about 18.7 m; the draft put it at the front's north-west corner under an eave about 16 m up
differences.how: T-2538: the tower stood at u 12.6 on the flank, 1.1 m proud as the sheet draws it, eaves 12.9 m, cone 5.8 m; its axis within about 20 px of the photograph's x 698, its apex within about 25 px

differences.what: the main block's height: two storeys of wall to a heavy cornice at about 8.1 m (principal floor 1.45 m up a stair of nine risers), the third storey in the roof; the draft stood three full storeys to an eave at about 12 m
differences.how: T-2538: principal floor 1.45 m, storeys 3.55 and 3.1 m to the cornice at 8.1 m

differences.what: the roof: very steep slate faces rising from the cornice to a flat deck ringed with cresting at about 16-19 m; the draft had a hip about 56 degrees off a 12 m eave
differences.how: T-2538: the builder's 72-degree mansard with a 7.2 m lower face and a low deck, its deck line within about 25 px of the photograph's

differences.what: the south pavilion: three storeys of wall at the south end of the front under a steep coped stone gable, its apex about 17 m
differences.how: T-2538: part p_south, three storeys to 13.9 m under a 58-degree gable facing the avenue; its gable within about 30 px of the photograph's

differences.what: the 18th Street flank: a three-storey section east of the tower and a gabled section beyond it, then a lower two-storey east range; the draft ran the whole flank at one height
differences.how: T-2538: parts p_flank and r3 at three storeys, r2 at two, eaves 13.9 and 8.1 m

differences.what: the east turret: a small round turret under a cone at the flank's north-east corner, its eaves about 8 m and its apex about 12.7 m; the draft had none
differences.how: T-2538: a 1.3 m turret on the sheet's second bump, eaves 8.1 m, cone to 12.8 m; its axis within about 20 px of the photograph's

differences.what: the corner entrance: an open loggia at the front's north-west corner, one round arch on each face, and a broad stair of about nine risers between curved cheek walls coming down the front; the build has a flat door and a straight stoop

the bowed bay in the middle of the front, two storeys under a balcony, and the front's openings: paired and mullioned windows in carved surrounds, the carved frieze over the principal storey; the build has the draft's evenly spaced sash. The sheet's bulge (v 4.8-10.2) and the photograph's bay (about 60 px further north) disagree about where it stands
all-stone walls: Bedford stone laid in courses on the front and the flank alike, with string courses and the corbel table; the build is the draft's flat stand-in stone
the tower's form: a shaft about 2.4 m across under a corbelled upper stage about 3.6 m across, its cone flaring from the stage; the build is one eight-sided prism 2.9 m across

the roof's dormers and deck: tall hooded dormers in the steep faces, the iron cresting and finials round the deck, the pavilion's and flank's tall stacks; the build's dormers sit sunk in the face and show only their gables, and it has no cresting
the gabled section on the flank: a gable facing 18th Street with a balcony at about 11.5 m; the build has a hip there
the south and east sides and the rear
differences.how: the camera looks from the north-west; T-2540 reads the HABS photographs for them
